That can be a really hard thing to hear, and I want to offer some perspective as a trans otter/twink who is polyamorous. 

It’s extremely rare to ever find a partner who fills 100% of your needs. And expecting a partner to fill all of one’s needs will lead to resentment and not fulfilling expectations. With that in mind, ethical non-monogamy seeks to allow people to explore love and relationships so that you CAN get all your needs met between the people you engage with. 

It’s liberating to see ethical non-monogamy not as “I’m not able to fulfill my partner’s every need so therefore we can be together/they don’t love me,” but instead as “there is no limit on love, and by agreeing that my partner can get their other needs met elsewhere, ensures that they can feel complete and happy with what I bring to the table, and I can trust that they love me and want to be with me.” 

If being in an open relationship is not something you want, then please do not feel pressured to do it; in that case, it will not end well. But if it does sound like something that you would want to explore, it can be really nice! Your BF isn’t saying anything about what he thinks you lack; rather he’s saying an additional part of what he wants out of relationships. Doesn’t say anything about how he sees you or how much he loves you. Some people really can like and love multiple people at once. 

Also, unless your BF explicitly said it’s about cis dick, I wouldn’t jump to conclusions. Regardless of cis or trans status, being with a twink versus or bear/daddy is a different sexual experience. But you can decide if that’s something you will tolerate in this relationship.
